newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares positive as floor trade opens.
newsitem.headline: German shares positive as floor trade opens.

text.p: German shares open bourse trade in positive territory on Wednesday, boosted by a stable dollar, firmer German bonds, a higher close on Wall St and gradually improving trading volumes.
In early bourse trade the DAX index, which measures floor trade in 30 blue-chip German equities, was up 7.66 points, or 0.30 percent, at 2,566.50 points.
"I don't expect us to move madly in the direction of 2,600 today. There is more going on, but we need more significant information to help us along," a Frankfurt trader said.
Sentiment on the floor of the Frankfurt stock exchange was improved in early trade, having been in the doldrums since trading volumes hit year lows of 2.4 billion marks on Monday.
An improvement in volumes to 5.23 billion marks on Tuesday was met with relief by German share traders, but they were still expecting narrow range trade between 2,600 and 2,700 points over the day.
Biggest trading volumes in early bourse trade were in chemical companies, with foreign investors seeking to line their portfolios with German chemical stocks.
BASF AG was up 12 pfennigs at 44.27 marks early on, while Hoechst AG was up 90 pfennigs at 53.05 marks. Bayer AG was up 14 pfennigs at 54.15 marks.
Carmaker Volkswagen was up 13 marks at 550 marks after it said its car deliveries in western Europe were up 11.3 percent to 1.451 million vehicles.
There was strong interest in industrial giant Daimler Benz early on, which was up 1.15 marks at 81.10 marks in advance of its first half figures which are due out on Thursday.
